summary: Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (1924–1981) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Karsé Kongtrul, the 13th Dalai Lama, Tubten Chokyi Dorje, and Karma Shedrub Chokyi Sengge.

Raniero Gnoli (1930–2025) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Giuseppe Tucci (~1948–1954) and Mario Praz, and served as Professor of Indology at Sapienza University of Rome from 1964 to 2000.
Ranu Kunwar is a PhD student at Australian National University (attested 2026), where she has studied under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron.

Raoul Birnbaum works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held posts as a professor of Buddhist studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz (attested 2003, 2017) and held an attested post at Santa Clara University in 2012.
Raphael Kühner (1802–1878) was a linguist. He was educated at Ernestinum Gotha and studied at the University of Göttingen (~1821–1824).

Raphael von Koeber (1848–1923) worked in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at the Moscow Conservatory (~1867–1872), Heidelberg University (~1873–1878), and the University of Jena (~1879–1881), and held a post at the University of Tokyo in 1893.

Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh (1897–1982) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He earned a BA at Fergusson College (~1914–1918) and served as Professor of Samskrta and Ancient Indian History at Gujarat Vidyapith (~1920–1930).

Rasmus Rask (1787–1832) worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at Odense Katedralskole and the University of Copenhagen, he held Copenhagen posts as librarian and professor of literary history (1825) and Eastern languages (1831).

Ratna Basu is an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1989 and holds a post as Professor (Special Invitee) at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Ratna Vajra Rinpoche (born 1974) is active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, whom he succeeded in 2017.

Ravi M. Gupta (born 1982) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned his DPhil at Oxford. He taught at William & Mary (~2008–2013) and became Charles Redd Chair of Religious Studies at Utah State University (~2013).

Ravindra Singh Bisht (born 1944) works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Lucknow and Kumaun University, serving as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (~1984–2004).

Rawi Bhavilai (1925–2017) was an academic in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned degrees from Chulalongkorn University, the University of Adelaide, and Australian National University, and served as a physics professor at Chulalongkorn University (1945–1986).

Raymond West (1832–1912) worked in Indology and studied under Martin Haug. His main posts included Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (~1878–1892) and Reader in Indian Law at the University of Cambridge (~1895–1907).
Reb Anderson (born 1943) is a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Richard Baker. He served as abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center from around 1986 to 1995.

Rebecca Hufen works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, she studied at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Dorji Wangchuk and served there as a lector for Tibetan Studies.

Rebecca Redwood French is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned a JD from the University of Washington and an LLM and PhD from Yale, later holding professorships at UC Boulder (attested 1996–2003) and University at Buffalo (attested 2014).
Rebecca Sundén works in Indology and Tibetology. Attested in 2026, she has studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin.

Reginald A. Ray (born 1942) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Mircea Eliade, among others. He taught at Naropa University as Professor in Buddhist Studies (attested 2001–2006) and at UC Boulder (attested 2001–2002).
Rei Yoshimura (born 1929) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University (~1949–1954) and later served as a professor there (~1974–2000).
